How this works. Nothing here is written yet — this is the raw material, quoted exactly from the sources, with every citation intact. Mark Keep for anything you want available when the articles get drafted, Maybe for anything worth a second look, and Cut for anything you have ruled out. Leaving something undecided is fine, and a passage you skip is simply not carried forward. Keyboard: J/K move, 1 keep, 2 maybe, 3 cut, 0 clear, / search.
One thing to watch as you read. Passages marked verify come from automated transcripts with a known defect — a garbled clause, a mishearing, in six cases a dropped negative that reverses the sense. Keep them if you want the substance, but the wording has to be checked against audio before it goes to print under anyone’s name.
Everything is here, including the ugly. Nothing has been withheld or hidden behind a filter. That includes the Victorian material on women, the harsher passages on sexuality, and the entries I would not put in a booklet myself — some of which are useful precisely as a foil, quoted to be answered. Where a passage came out of a section I had flagged in review, the line under it names that section, so you can see what I thought and disagree with it.

Round one of two. Marks save automatically and are shared — there is nothing to export or send. When the team is done, the selections are read straight out and the articles get drafted from them. Full manuscripts for every passage are in the corpus bundle; every citation here points back into it.
